hero.name: Serigne Khalifa Ababacar Sy Nguirane
hero.tagline: I don’t just design screens: I design products that people understand and actually use. I help companies turn a need into a high-impact digital solution, through a rigorous, user-centered approach.

servicesPreview.title: My services
servicesPreview.intro: I help companies design modern, user-centered technology. My way of working is rooted in a user-centered approach: understanding people’s needs, frustrations and expectations to design experiences that are both simple and impactful.

aboutPreview.photoAlt: Portrait of Serigne Khalifa Ababacar Sy Nguirane, smiling, in a white shirt with arms crossed
aboutPreview.text: With a degree in computer science, I started out in development, with plenty of curiosity and little experience. Then came a moment of doubt: what should I specialize in? I looked at what truly defines me: I am organized, very attentive to detail, and I like to think before I act. Those traits naturally led me to front-end, where I quickly realized I was missing a real sense of usability. That is when I discovered Figma, and with it an immediate ease in building mockups. I trained, and realized that UX design is not just about drawing: it is about understanding user behavior to design products that genuinely serve them. Little by little, my interest widened from UX to product design, with a more holistic view of the product. Today, I have a clear direction, many projects behind me, and I am more ready than ever to go further.

method.title: 4 essential pillars
method.imageAlt: Serigne Khalifa Ababacar Sy Nguirane, thoughtful, hand on chin, in front of the words product and user research

understand.title: Understand
understand.text: I pin down the business need, the goals and the context of the project.

listen.title: Listen
listen.text: I talk with users and stakeholders, and observe real-world usage.

test.title: Test
test.text: I validate my choices on a prototype before any code is written.

build.title: Deliver
build.text: I design the final mockups and prepare the handoff to developers.

mobile.title: Mobile app design
mobile.description: Clear, enjoyable iOS and Android apps built for real-world use: smooth flows, readable interfaces and consistent components.

web.title: Web app design
web.description: Modern, responsive websites and web apps, from information architecture to high-fidelity mockups ready for development.

research.title: User research & UX audit
research.description: Interviews, usability tests and UX audits to understand your users and pinpoint what is holding your product back.

prototype.title: Prototyping & design systems
prototype.description: Interactive prototypes to test ideas fast, and design systems to keep the interface consistent as the product grows.

example.title: A concrete example
example.text: It all starts with a sheet of paper and a pencil. These sketches lay down the essentials: where the user searches, how they pick a destination, how they talk with their assistant. Once the structure is validated, it becomes a clear interface: a simple search, destinations within thumb’s reach, and two ways to talk with the assistant, by message or by voice. Same journey, same logic, but designed to be understood at first glance.
example.stepsLabel: From problem to interface: persona, sketches, mockups
example.personaAlt: Persona Awa, smiling, phone in hand at a café terrace in Dakar. Problem: Awa wants to discover places and activities without spending much, but she lacks reliable information, prices are not transparent, and organizing transport outside Dakar is difficult, which discourages her. Hypothesis: if the app offers places sorted by budget, Awa will easily find affordable activities; if prices are clear with promotions/deals, Awa will be more motivated to go out.
example.sketchesAlt: Pencil sketches of two Samba app screens: the home screen with search, filters and a destination card, then the assistant chat screen (message or voice) with its history
example.screensAlt: Final Samba app mockups: the home screen “Choose your next destination” featuring Lac Rose, and the message or voice chat screen with Samba and its history

sengame.title: SenGame
sengame.summary: A mobile app to buy gaming equipment in Senegal
sengame.coverAlt: Three screens of the SenGame mobile app: shopping cart, catalog and home page

slides.s1: Cover: SenGame, a gaming equipment sales application, illustrated by a robot wearing a VR headset
slides.s2: Three SenGame screens: shopping cart, catalog and home page “Discover the best e-gaming products in Senegal”
slides.s3: Project overview: a mobile app for video game enthusiasts, 1.5-month project, problem “how to buy gaming products online?”, role of UX designer
slides.s4: User research: secondary research based on data collected by Game Hub Senegal
slides.s5: Pain points: 60% of players in Senegal do not spend money on gaming, most have no bank card, and difficult navigation makes people give up
slides.s6: Persona Matar, 22, student in Dakar, passionate about video games: wants to buy gaming equipment, skeptical about online shopping
slides.s7: Persona Sokhna, 38, entrepreneur and mother of two: wants to buy games for her children, has little knowledge of video games and e-commerce
slides.s8: User journey map for Matar: choose a product, view the cart, validate the purchase and track the order, with tasks, emotions and improvements
slides.s9: User journey map for Sokhna: the same four steps, with suggestions added to guide her choice
slides.s10: Hand-drawn storyboard: Matar is bored at home, downloads SenGame, picks equipment, waits for delivery and is happy to play
slides.s11: User flow for buying equipment: home, catalog or search, product, cart, validation, payment
slides.s12: Information architecture: home, account, catalog, cart and other sections with their sub-pages
slides.s13: Paper wireframes of the home, catalog and cart pages
slides.s14: Digital wireframes of the home, catalog and cart pages made in Figma
slides.s15: Mockups of the home, catalog and cart pages
slides.s16: Catalog mockup: search bar, filters (new, popular, promo), latest collections and categories
slides.s17: Shopping cart mockup: product cards with quantity, total and “Validate purchase” button
slides.s18: Product details mockup: PlayStation 5 with photo carousel, rating, description and “Buy now” button
slides.s19: Splash screen, onboarding “The video game market, simple and secure” and login screen
slides.s20: Search screen with game categories, “My hub” for order tracking and articles, and add a bank card screen

waterflow.title: Waterflow
waterflow.summary: A dashboard to monitor connected drinking-water dispensers in real time
waterflow.coverAlt: Waterflow: the Dispensers page (list and map) and the Dashboard page (KPIs, volume of water distributed and heatmap) of the platform

slides.s1: Cover: Waterflow use case, a mother giving her baby a glass of water
slides.s2: Project overview: transforming access to drinking water in West Africa with terracotta filters made by women artisans, IoT dispensers and an internal platform
slides.s3: Design process: discovery, define, wireframe & design, test, and the tools used (Figma, Notion, Miro, Jira, ChatGPT)
slides.s4: Persona Fama, 40, operations manager at Anilaye’O in Thiès: wants a clear view of performance and real-time alerts, frustrated by late alerts and manual follow-up
slides.s5: Persona Amadou, 28, maintenance technician in Thiès: wants to quickly spot faulty dispensers and receive real-time alerts
slides.s6: Empathy map of Fama (says, thinks, does, feels), with the problem statement and the assumption
slides.s7: “How might we” questions and selected ideas: real-time status of dispensers, a map of their locations and simpler graphs
slides.s8: Sitemap: login, dashboard, users, dispensers, revenue, notifications, settings and task tracking
slides.s9: Style guide: Outfit typography scale, brand colors and state colors
slides.s10: Login screen of the Waterflow platform
slides.s11: Dashboard: KPIs (active and inactive dispensers, ongoing alerts), volume of water distributed and a heatmap of the usage rate by region
slides.s12: Dispensers page: search bar, list of dispensers with their status (active, maintenance, out of order) and a map
slides.s13: Thank you: the Anilaye’O website and the Revenue, Users and Maintenance pages of the dashboard
